title: Continuous maps into totally disconnected spaces descend through components
statement: Use the universe convention of [def-weil-size-convention], with the spaces and function sets formed in the containing universe. Let $T,B$ be arbitrary topological spaces, and suppose $B$ is totally disconnected, meaning that every connected subset has at most one point. Let $\pi_0(T)$ be the quotient by belonging to the same connected component (maximal connected subset), with the quotient topology, and let $q_T:T\to\pi_0(T)$ be the quotient map. The map $q_T$ is continuous and surjective. For every continuous $f:T\to B$ there is a continuous $\bar f:\pi_0(T)\to B$ satisfying $\bar f\circ q_T=f$; any function $v:\pi_0(T)\to B$ satisfying $v\circ q_T=f$ equals $\bar f$. Empty spaces are allowed.
